content:
According to the latest report from Bloomberg, Apple is developing a screenless health and fitness tracker to compete with Whoop. The company is reportedly "developing prototypes," but has yet to decide whether to officially release the product.

The internal prototype is said to feature a "slim fabric strap with a built-in sensor computing module." The project is currently in the "technical exploration" phase, with Bloomberg indicating the product is unlikely to launch until after 2028, assuming Apple ultimately decides to release it.

The project reportedly has the support of Apple executives, including Eddy Cue and Tim Cook. Cue took over Apple's health team last October following Jeff Williams' departure.

Products like Whoop and Oura Ring are popular among users who don't want to wear a smartwatch but still want to track health and fitness data. According to Reuters, Oura is preparing for an IPO and recently disclosed that it sold 3.6 million Oura Rings in the 12 months ending June 30. Revenue grew 74% to $1.21 billion in the nine months ending June 30.

However, Apple remains dominant in the smartwatch market. Apple Watch offers far more features than health-and-fitness-focused wearables like Oura and Whoop.
